name: Transformer scratch
lesson:
## Drag with the fader chopping over it

A two-beat forward drag and a two-beat back drag per bar, while the crossfader clicks open and closed on every sixteenth: sixteen clicks over each stroke. The platter hand is slow and even, the fader hand is fast and even, and they do not listen to each other.

Studio Scratches' transformer tutorial is this exact exercise: the fader does a rhythm, the platter provides a long tone for the rhythm to cut up. It is the hardest independence exercise in basic scratching because the two hands have different tempos. If the drag speeds up whenever the clicks start, slow the whole thing down until it does not.

tracks.cue: The 'ahhh' and 'fresh' vocoder samples: cue on the 'ahhh'. Scratch material, so tempo and key are not matched.
Skipless locked grooves so the sample never has to be re-cued.
B: two-beat drags with the crossfader clicking on every sixteenth.
